title: UPI market leader PhonePe becomes a public company ahead of IPO
summary: PhonePe has converted from a private to a public company as a preparatory legal step ahead of a planned initial public offering. The Bengaluru-based, Walmart-owned digital payments firm has appointed major global bankers and seeks a valuation of up to $15 billion. PhonePe leads India’s UPI market with roughly 48% share and reported strong FY24 financials, with revenue up 73% and PAT turning positive.
content:
PhonePe, the Walmart-owned digital payments platform, has formally transitioned from a private firm to a public company in advance of a planned initial public offering (IPO), the company told the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The move is a necessary legal step for firms seeking to list on Indian stock markets. PhonePe said it began preparatory steps for a potential IPO on February 20 and selected Kotak Mahindra Capital, JP Morgan, Citi and Morgan Stanley as advisers, with reports indicating the company may seek a valuation of up to $15 billion.

An extraordinary general meeting held on April 16 resolved to change the company name from "PhonePe Private Limited" to "PhonePe Limited", according to a document submitted to the RoC and shared with Moneycontrol by private company data platform The Kredible. The company noted that the change is subject to approval by the Central Processing Centre, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, which must issue a fresh certificate of incorporation.

PhonePe redomiciled from Singapore to India in December 2022 and said it has established a clear corporate structure, designating each of its non-payment businesses as fully owned subsidiaries. The company cited strong top-line and bottom-line growth across a diverse business portfolio, as detailed in its FY23-24 annual report, as reasons this is an opportune time to prepare for a public listing.

In its last private fundraising, PhonePe was valued at about $12 billion. Media reports have since linked the company with bankers and advisers as it prepares for a potential public debut and a higher target valuation.

The Bengaluru-based company is the largest player in India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) ecosystem, with roughly 48% market share. Google Pay is the second-largest platform with about 37%.

PhonePe delivered robust financial performance in FY24, reporting a 73% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 5,064 crore. Profit after tax (PAT) was Rs 197 crore, a turnaround from a loss of Rs 738 crore in the previous year.

The company’s strategic corporate changes, redomiciliation and improved financials appear aligned with its stated intention to pursue a listing, but the formal name change and public company status still require statutory approvals from Indian authorities.

## Transition to a Public Company

The move is a necessary legal step for firms seeking to list on Indian stock markets. PhonePe said it began preparatory steps for a potential IPO on February 20 and selected Kotak Mahindra Capital, JP Morgan, Citi and Morgan Stanley as advisers, with reports indicating the company may seek a valuation of up to $15 billion.

## Corporate Name Change

An extraordinary general meeting held on April 16 resolved to change the company name from “PhonePe Private Limited” to “PhonePe Limited”, according to a document submitted to the RoC and shared with Moneycontrol by private company data platform The Kredible. The company noted that the change is subject to approval by the Central Processing Centre, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, which must issue a fresh certificate of incorporation.

## Corporate Structure and Redomiciliation

PhonePe redomiciled from Singapore to India in December 2022 and said it has established a clear corporate structure, designating each of its non-payment businesses as fully owned subsidiaries. The company cited strong top-line and bottom-line growth across a diverse business portfolio, as detailed in its FY23-24 annual report, as reasons this is an opportune time to prepare for a public listing.

## Valuation and Advisers

In its last private fundraising, PhonePe was valued at about $12 billion. Media reports have since linked the company with bankers and advisers as it prepares for a potential public debut and a higher target valuation.

- Selected advisers: Kotak Mahindra Capital, JP Morgan, Citi, Morgan Stanley
- Potential target valuation reported: up to $15 billion

## Market Position

The Bengaluru-based company is the largest player in India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) ecosystem, with roughly 48% market share. Google Pay is the second-largest platform with about 37%.

## Financial Performance

PhonePe delivered robust financial performance in FY24:

- Revenue: Rs 5,064 crore (up 73% year-on-year)
- Profit after tax (PAT): Rs 197 crore (a turnaround from a loss of Rs 738 crore the previous year)
